name: widget-grid
summary: A live draggable / droppable / resizable dashboard grid — the framework-agnostic answer to vue-grid-layout. Slot in obs-widget-card children carrying data-x/data-y/data-w/data-h; the grid snaps each to a 12-column layout, pushes colliding cards down, compacts everything up under gravity, and auto-scrolls the page while you drag or resize a card past the fold. Emits layout-change with the settled positions.
selectHint: Reach for this when a user must arrange their OWN dashboard — drag cards around, resize them, and have the layout persist. If the layout is fixed and authored by you (never rearranged at runtime), use a plain CSS grid instead — this element carries drag/resize/collision machinery you don't need.
whenToUse: A user-arrangeable board of widgets — a monitoring dashboard, a report canvas, any surface where the end user drags and resizes cards and you save where they land.
insteadOf: a hand-rolled absolute-position + pointer-math drag layer
a static CSS grid when you actually need runtime rearrange/resize

variants.name: 12-column (default)
variants.what: columns="12" — the product's standard dashboard grid; cards placed on a 12-wide unit lattice.

variants.name: custom columns
variants.what: Any column count (e.g. columns="6" for a denser, coarser board or a narrow panel).

variants.name: custom cell height / gap
variants.what: cell-height and gap tune row height and the space between cards without touching card markup.

sizes.name: cell-height
sizes.note: Row unit height in px; a card's rendered height = h × cell-height + (h−1) × gap.

sizes.name: gap
sizes.note: Gutter in px between cells, applied on both axes.

sizes.name: width
sizes.note: Column width is computed from the host's measured width via a ResizeObserver — the grid is fluid; give it a block container to fill.

states.name: idle
states.what: Cards sit at their compacted grid positions; each transitions smoothly (transform/width/height .15s) when the layout shifts.

states.name: dragging a card
states.what: On a card's card-dragstart the grid follows the pointer in 'move' mode: the live card lifts (z-index 50, no transition), a dashed placeholder shows the target cell, colliding cards push down, and everything compacts up under the moved card.

states.name: resizing a card
states.what: On card-resizestart the grid runs 'resize' mode: the card grows from its bottom-right corner, snapping w to remaining columns and h up to a safety cap (MAX_H = 40 rows); the placeholder previews the new footprint and neighbours reflow.

states.name: auto-scrolling
states.what: When the pointer sits in the top/bottom 48px edge band during a drag/resize, the nearest scrollable ancestor scrolls (20px/frame) and the drag math is compensated by how far it has scrolled — so a card can be dragged or grown past the current viewport fold.

columns.note: Number of grid columns. Cards' data-x/data-w are in these column units. Coerced to a number; falls back to 12 if invalid.

cellHeight.note: Attribute: cell-height. Row unit height in px. A card of height h renders h × cell-height + (h−1) × gap px tall. Falls back to 80 if invalid.

gap.note: Gutter in px between cells on both axes. Column width = (containerWidth − (columns−1) × gap) / columns. Falls back to 10 if invalid.

events.name: layout-change
events.detail: Array of { x, y, w, h } — one entry per obs-widget-card in DOM order, the settled grid positions after a drag or resize completes (pointerup).
events.note: Fired once per gesture, on drop. The grid also writes the new values back onto each card's data-x/data-y/data-w/data-h attributes, so you can persist either the event payload or read the attributes. Use it to save the board and to reflow chart widgets that only auto-size on width.

slots.default: obs-widget-card children, each with data-x / data-y / data-w / data-h attributes (column/row origin + width/height in grid units; defaults 0/0/4/3 if omitted). The grid assigns every card an internal `slot="cN"` and positions it via a wrapper in its own shadow DOM — never position or transform a card yourself. A MutationObserver re-syncs when cards are added or removed.

decisionFlow: Does the END USER rearrange the layout at runtime (drag cards, resize them, and expect it to stick)? -> obs-widget-grid.
Is the layout authored by YOU and never rearranged by the user? -> a static CSS grid (display:grid) — don't pull in drag/resize machinery you won't use.
Do you just need ONE resizable/movable panel (not a board of them)? -> a split/panel primitive, not a grid.

Building the children: each widget is an obs-widget-card (it emits card-dragstart from its header and card-resizestart from its bottom-right handle — that's what the grid listens for). Give the grid a block container with a real width so column math resolves.
Need cards draggable past the fold? -> the grid already auto-scrolls the nearest scrollable ancestor; just make sure that ancestor is the scroll container (overflow:auto/scroll).

12-column (default).useWhen: you want the product's standard board — leave columns at 12 so every widget's data-x/data-w reads on the same lattice the rest of the product uses, and cards line up across dashboards
12-column (default).dontUse: the surface is a narrow panel or a wide wall where 12 units are too fine or too coarse (drop to a custom column count instead)
12-column (default).example: <obs-widget-grid> (no columns attr) wrapping the Alert-Summary gauges, heatmap and pie cards on the default 12-wide grid
12-column (default).asSeenIn: the Alert-Summary dashboard board (the default obs-widget-grid, 12 columns)

custom columns.useWhen: the board's width or density needs a different lattice — columns="6" for a narrow side panel, a higher count for a wide wall board — so card footprints snap sensibly to the available width
custom columns.dontUse: the placement expresses cleanly on 12 columns (keep it 12 for cross-dashboard consistency)
custom columns.example: <obs-widget-grid columns="6"> for a compact side panel of stat cards
custom columns.asSeenIn: a compact side panel of stat cards on a 6-column grid

custom cell height / gap.useWhen: the widget density on this board needs taller/shorter rows or tighter/looser gutters grid-wide — set cell-height and gap once instead of resizing every card
custom cell height / gap.dontUse: only one card needs to be taller (change that card's data-h — cell-height/gap are grid-wide, not per-card)
custom cell height / gap.example: <obs-widget-grid cell-height="78" gap="10"> to match the Alert-Summary row rhythm
custom cell height / gap.asSeenIn: the Alert-Summary board tuned with cell-height="78" gap="10"

user-arrangeable-dashboard.useWhen: the user builds/edits their own board — drag widgets, resize them, and you save the layout
user-arrangeable-dashboard.dontUse: the layout is fixed and code-authored (use a CSS grid) — the drag/resize/collision logic is dead weight there
user-arrangeable-dashboard.example: the Alert-Summary board: gauges, an infrastructure heatmap and pie widgets the user hand-arranges
user-arrangeable-dashboard.asSeenIn: the Alert-Summary dashboard (the whole board is one obs-widget-grid of obs-widget-card children)

custom-columns.useWhen: a denser or coarser lattice suits the surface — columns="6" for a narrow panel, more columns for a wide wall board
custom-columns.dontUse: you can express the placement on the standard 12-column grid (keep it 12 for product consistency)
custom-columns.example: a compact side panel of stat cards on a 6-column grid

cell-height-gap.useWhen: you need taller rows or tighter/looser gutters for the widget density on this board
cell-height-gap.dontUse: resizing an individual card would do (that's the card's h, not a grid-wide change)
cell-height-gap.example: cell-height="78" gap="10" on the Alert-Summary board

do: Make every child an obs-widget-card with data-x / data-y / data-w / data-h (column/row origin + size in grid units).
Give the grid a block container with a real width — column width is measured from it via ResizeObserver.
Ensure the intended scroll container (the ancestor with overflow:auto/scroll) is the one that scrolls, so edge auto-scroll can drag cards past the fold.
Listen to layout-change to persist the board and to reflow chart widgets (e.g. Highcharts only auto-sizes on width, so reflow taller cards on the size change).
Let the grid own positioning — read the settled positions from the event detail or the cards' data-* attributes after a gesture.
dont: Don't nest a widget grid inside another widget grid.
Don't position or transform the cards yourself (set left/top/transform) — the grid places each one via its own shadow-DOM wrapper; positioning a slotted element directly is buggy across browsers.
Don't put non-obs-widget-card elements as direct children expecting placement — only obs-widget-card children are synced into items.
Don't fight the compaction — cards gravity-compact upward; encode intent in data-x/data-y, not in CSS.

a11y.summary: A pointer-driven drag/resize surface — flag the keyboard gap honestly. The grid moves and sizes cards from pointermove/pointerup, driven by card-dragstart / card-resizestart (pointer gestures on the card); it does not currently expose a keyboard path for rearranging or resizing, nor announce gesture state to assistive tech. Positioning is presentational, so a board stays READABLE by content even though it is not REARRANGEABLE by keyboard.
issues: No keyboard alternative for drag/move or resize — rearranging is pointer-only (card-dragstart / card-resizestart come from pointer interactions).
Drag/resize state is not announced to assistive technology — no aria-live feedback on move, resize, or drop.
The dashed placeholder is a purely visual affordance (aria-hidden by nature) — an AT user gets no equivalent preview of where a card will land.
Edge auto-scroll moves content under the pointer only; there is no keyboard-triggered scroll-into-view for an off-screen card during a (would-be) keyboard rearrange.
a11y.notes: Positioning is presentational — assistive tech reads each card's own content, not the visual grid coordinates. Mitigations today: (1) give every obs-widget-card a real title so the board is navigable by content; (2) ship a sensible DEFAULT layout so a keyboard/AT user is never forced to rearrange to reach content; (3) treat rearrangement as an enhancement over an already-usable static reading order. A keyboard rearrange affordance (arrow-key move, Shift+arrow resize, each step re-compacting + firing layout-change, announced via an aria-live region) is a known gap for a future revision.

knownIssues: Keyboard-only users cannot rearrange or resize cards — the gesture is pointer-driven (card-dragstart / card-resizestart come from pointer interactions on the card).

Resize height is capped at MAX_H = 40 rows — a safety cap so a held auto-scroll during resize can't grow a card without bound; a card cannot be resized taller than 40 row-units regardless of drag distance.

Edge auto-scroll targets the NEAREST scrollable ancestor (first ancestor with overflow-y auto/scroll AND real overflow); if the real scroll container isn't a scrollable ancestor of the grid, dragging past the fold falls back to the document scroller and may not move the intended region.

Only direct obs-widget-card children are managed; other elements slotted in are ignored by the layout engine (not positioned, not compacted) — put charts/gauges/heatmaps INSIDE a card's default slot, not as grid children.

Column width is measured from the host via ResizeObserver, so the grid must have a real, non-zero rendered width before cards can be placed sensibly (an unsized/display:none container collapses cellW to its 1px floor).

Chart widgets that only auto-size on width (e.g. Highcharts) leave empty space below a card that was resized TALLER — reflow them from the layout-change event (and/or a per-card ResizeObserver), the grid does not reflow card bodies for you.
Nesting a widget grid inside another widget grid is unsupported — the inner grid's cards would be double-managed.
changelog: 2026-09-07 — Added obs-widget-grid: live drag/drop/resize dashboard grid — grid snap, collision push-down, gravity-up compaction, edge auto-scroll with scroll-compensated drag math, layout-change events. Positions obs-widget-card children (data-x/y/w/h) via shadow-DOM wrappers + named slots. Powers the Alert-Summary board.
